text:
maria: FYI customer on Dedicated is seeing intermittent 429s during a nightly batch. They say they were within their reserved pool qps, but traffic spiked briefly. Billing also shows a burst of usage. Can we triage?
aj: Which customer / pool id? any repro steps or request ids?
maria: Org 7892, pool eu-west-1-03. They ran a bulk inference job at 02:10 UTC. Attach from customer: 
```
2026-03-16T02:10:12Z request_id=cf1a2 status=429 model=moss-13b-temp
2026-03-16T02:10:15Z request_id=cf1a3 status=200 model=moss-13b-temp
```
ben: Ops alert also fired: ops-bot: "reserved-pool-eu-west-1-03 headroom < 10% for 18s" around same time.
liza: Could be token-bucket refill misalignment if their client had a bursty connect pattern. Any auth failures?
maria: Customer logs show a short auth retry loop (token refresh) around 02:10 but most requests had valid tokens. They reported 429s for ~25s window.
aj: Also check rate-limiter sharding — if their traffic concentrated on a single shard we could hit per-shard cap even if pool overall has headroom. Can platform logs show shard distribution?
ben: I pulled router logs: 
```
[2026-03-16T02:10:11Z] pool=eu-west-1-03 shard=7 org=7892 req=cf1a2 status=429 reason=rate_limit_shard
[2026-03-16T02:10:13Z] pool=eu-west-1-03 shard=7 org=7892 req=cf1a3 status=200
```
liza: That points at shard hot-spotting. Could be client connection reuse pattern pinned to one node. Did they use streaming vs non-streaming?
maria: Bulk job used many concurrent short-lived connections (python requests) with keepalive off. They said they parallelized across 64 workers.
aj: Ah — many short TCP sessions can land on same upstream due to L4 hashing. If upstream instance's token bucket exhausted, you'll see 429s while other instances idle. Need to confirm per-instance token buckets at that time.
ben: I can fetch instance token-bucket counters for shard=7 at 02:10. Give me a minute.
ops-bot: Incident note created: INC-2026-7892-reserved-pool-429s. Auto-tag priority=P2.
ben: Counters: shard-7 tokens consumed surge -> bucket drained at 02:10:10, refill rate normal but small headroom. Matches 25s window.
liza: Root cause hypothesis: client connection pattern + L4 hashing -> shard hotspot -> per-shard token bucket exhaustion -> 429s for short window. Auth retries might have amplified load.
aj: Short-term mitigation: advise customer to enable connection pooling/keep-alive or reduce concurrency, or we can rotate their traffic across more shards by adjusting flow-hash knobs for their pool.
maria: Customer asked if we can retroactively credit them for failed requests; billing shows 110 failed requests charged.
enforcement: We must check billing policy for reserved pool 429s. Who handles credits?
ben: Support can request billing credit for confirmed platform-side rate limits. I need exact request_ids and timeframe. We have the logs and ops-bot incident.
liza: Also suggest we add a platform guard: detect short-lived connection flood and prefer per-org round-robin at L7 fallback to avoid single-shard pressure. I'll file a runtime infra ticket.
aj: For immediate repro steps for ENG-ML and ENG-RUNTIME: 
1) Run a script simulating 64 workers with keepalive=false hitting the dedicated endpoint for org=7892.
2) Observe per-shard token consumption via /internal/telemetry endpoint: `curl -s http://telemetry.local/pools/eu-west-1-03/shards`
3) Collect router logs filter org=7892 and timestamp range 02:09:50-02:10:40.
(we should not share internal endpoints with customer)
maria: I'll send the mitigation suggestions to the customer and ask for permission to run a controlled repro with them later today. Also requesting billing credit path.
ben: I'll attach the shard logs and token bucket counters to the incident.
ops-bot: ops-bot: "linked INC-2026-7892-reserved-pool-429s -> runbook reserved-pool-hotspot"
liza: Follow-up items for infra: (a) evaluate L4 hashing diversification, (b) alerting: trigger reserved-pool-hotspot alert earlier when per-shard imbalance > 3x.
aj: Thanks everyone. If customer agrees to repro, assign me and ben for live triage.
maria: Customer replied: "please try repro, we'll stand by. we can also enable keepalive on our side but need your guidance." I'll coordinate. :thumbsup:
ben: Marking this resolved-on-support-side for now, leaving incident open for infra follow-up.
maria: Closing loop with customer once infra has proposed longer-term fix.
